name: PT Bank Neo Commerce Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Neo Commerce: a capital-rich digital bank priced for a credit cycle it is not having
frontmatter.summary: BBYB is a profitable, heavily capitalised digital bank whose shares trade far below book. FY2025 net profit was IDR565.7bn on a 14.5% ROE, yet the market capitalises only a fraction of the franchise. Our base case values the bank well above the price; the controlling shareholder's intentions and governance are the swing risks.
thesis: A profitable digital bank at a fraction of book: FY2025 net profit of IDR565.7bn and ROE of 14.5% [S19], against a share price of Rp157 and FY2026E P/B of 0.4x.
Capital is not the constraint: CAR reached 53.4% and core capital IDR4,350.0bn at Sep-2026 [S2], funding a deliberately shrinking, higher-quality loan book rather than a growth-at-all-costs model.
Our most-likely case gives a twelve-month value of Rp376 (139.3%); the dividend-only DDM alone is worth well above today's price, so the market is not even paying for the distribution stream.
The controlling shareholder is the swing factor: Akulaku group control, a new president director and a FY2025 profit retained in full to rebuild capital, with no dividend yet announced [S6][S8][S12].
Macro is a headwind, not the thesis: the house is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive banks, but this is a balance-sheet-value call, not a NIM-beta trade.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results and the first full year of the new president director's strategy
AGM decision on the FY2026 profit and the first indication of a dividend or capital-return policy
OJK fit-and-proper approval of the new directors and any follow-on governance changes
BNPL and fee-income ramp; CASA and cost-to-income evidence

blocks.text: We initiate Bank Neo Commerce (BBYB) at BUY with a twelve-month value of Rp376, 139.3% above the Rp157 price. The variant view is simple: the market is valuing a licensed, profitable and heavily over-capitalised digital bank as if its earnings were about to disappear. The shares change hands at 0.4x FY2026E book and 3.8x FY2026E earnings, while the bank earned IDR565.7bn in FY2025, holds equity of IDR4,230.7bn and a CAR of 53.4% [S19][S2]. Our residual-income, justified P/BV and DDM methods all land near book value, well above the current price.

What the market appears to price is the end of the earnings stream, not a slower one. At Rp157 the implied sustainable return on equity is roughly the dividend-only value, which captures none of the retained earnings compounding book value. The gap closes only if the bank keeps earning a return near its cost of equity on a much larger book; that is what our base case assumes and what the bear case tests.

Three things move the value. First, credit cost: FY2025 and 9M2026 provisioning was unusually benign, and the base case normalises it rather than extrapolating zero. Second, the funding mix: CASA rose to 33.0% of deposits, and whether that holds against deposit competition sets the NIM path. Third, governance and control: Akulaku group's intentions, the new management team and a fully retained FY2025 profit [S6][S8].

Bank Neo Commerce is an Indonesian digital bank. It takes retail deposits through its neobank app and lends to consumers and micro, small and medium enterprises, alongside transaction, wealth-management and payment services. The product set spans savings and time deposits, consumer and micro business loans, transfers, QRIS payments, virtual accounts and mutual-fund distribution [S0][S18]. The bank is a challenger, not a scale incumbent: it employs 909.0 people and carries a market capitalisation of IDR2,096.0bn on 157.0 per share [S0].

The revenue model is high-margin, high-yield lending funded by a deposit franchise. At Sep-2026 gross loans were IDR6,730.0bn, down from IDR7,180.0bn at Dec-2025, against third-party funds of IDR11,860.0bn [S2][S19]. Net interest income was IDR2,348.8bn in FY2025, with non-interest income of IDR159.0bn [S0]. The loan mix is deliberate: consumer and UMKM lending reached IDR5,800.0bn at Jun-2026, growing year on year, while the commercial and corporate book was cut to protect asset quality [S21][S2].

Strategy is explicitly "quality growth" rather than volume. Management is prioritising selective consumer and UMKM lending, deposit repricing, fee income from payments and a planned BNPL product, and operating-cost discipline [S19][S21]. The deliberate contraction is visible in the numbers: loans fell -18.6% in FY2025 and were still IDR7,180.0bn at Dec-2025, while deposits rose to IDR14,030.0bn [S19]. The bank is choosing margin and asset quality over balance-sheet growth, which is the right choice when capital is abundant and the credit cycle is uncertain.

The product shelf is broad for a bank of this size. On the deposit side it runs the Rekening Neo current account, regular and thematic savings products, and the WOW and FLEXI time-deposit lines; on the asset side it offers Neo Pinjam consumer credit and micro-business loans; and the payments and services layer covers transfers, QRIS, virtual accounts, bill payments, cardless cash withdrawal, membership and gamification, wealth management and branch services [S18]. Corporate customers are served through current accounts, time deposits and lending [S18]. That breadth matters for the thesis because fee income and CASA are the two levers that do not require balance-sheet growth, and both depend on transaction engagement rather than on the size of the loan book.

The franchise is a genuine app-first bank rather than a digital window on a branch network. Distribution is through the neobank application and a limited branch and service footprint, which is why the cost base can scale with customers rather than with locations [S18]. The trade-off is that customer acquisition is bought with marketing and deposit pricing, and the app must keep earning engagement against e-wallets and larger digital banks. We treat the app franchise and the listed currency as the durable assets, and the capital surplus as the buffer that lets management be patient while the credit book is rebuilt [S19].

Control sits with the Akulaku group, described in company communications as the bank's owner [S6]. Gozco Capital held 10.5% in Feb-2026 [S5], and insiders as a group hold 58.9% of the shares, with a free float of 48.3% [S0]; the two provider figures are struck on different bases and do not sum to the whole, so we use them as indicative of concentration, not as an ownership reconciliation. The state connection is indirect: the bank is licensed and supervised by OJK and Bank Indonesia and is a member of the deposit-insurance scheme [S18].

Indonesian banking is a large, under-penetrated market where the digital channel is growing faster than the branch model. The house macro deck has real GDP growth at 5.3% and CPI at 3.3%, with the policy rate at 5.8% [S0]. That combination supports nominal credit growth but also keeps deposit competition intense, which is the central industry tension for a small digital bank: the loan yield is high, but the funding cost is set by larger competitors and by the rate cycle.

A digital bank earns its return by borrowing short (deposits) and lending longer at higher rates (consumer and small-business credit). Because it has no legacy branch network, its cost base is mostly technology and marketing rather than property and staff, but it also lacks the cheap current-account balances that an incumbent collects from corporate relationships. The model therefore lives or dies on two things: the deposit franchise (how cheap and sticky its funding is) and credit discipline (how much of the high headline yield survives loan losses). Scale helps both, which is why most digital banks spend years losing money before they reach a sustainable return.

The competitive set is crowded. SeaBank, Bank Jago, Allo Bank, Superbank and the digital arms of larger groups all compete for the same retail deposits and consumer-loan customers. BBYB's differentiation is a long-standing app franchise, a listed currency and, unusually, a very large capital surplus: CAR of 53.4% versus the regulatory minimum is far above what a growing bank needs [S2]. That surplus is a moat in a downturn — it lets the bank absorb losses and keep lending — but it is also a drag on ROE while it sits idle.

The industry's structure matters more than its headline growth for a bank this size. Indonesian banking is segmented by capital tier and by customer franchise: the large state and private banks set deposit pricing, the digital challengers compete for the same mass-market savers, and the regulator is deliberately pushing consolidation among smaller institutions. BBYB sits in the digital challenger tier: too small to set funding prices, large enough in capital to survive a squeeze, and therefore a price-taker on deposits and a price-maker only in the niches where its app reaches customers its competitors do not [S2][S19].

That position explains the deposit strategy. Management cut expensive time deposits and grew savings, lifting CASA to 33.0% by Sep-2026, which is the only durable way for a price-taker to protect a high NIM [S2]. It also explains why the loan book was cut: in a crowded consumer-credit market, the marginal loan is only worth making if the risk-adjusted spread clears a normalised credit cost, and the bank chose to shrink rather than defend volume [S19][S21]. For a challenger, that discipline is a competitive behaviour, not a retreat.

On the five forces, the threat of new entrants is high but the licence and capital requirements are real barriers; supplier power is low; buyer power is high because depositors can move money with a tap; the threat of substitutes is high from e-wallets and fintech lenders; and rivalry is intense. The moat is therefore narrow: a licence, a brand and a capital cushion, not a structural cost advantage. Regulation is the other force: OJK sets capital, liquidity and governance standards, and compliance failures carry franchise risk even when they do not touch the core licence. In March 2026 OJK cancelled the registration of the bank's institutional securities marketing-partner programme; the bank said operations were unaffected [S23]. We treat that as a governance signal rather than a solvency event.

The five-year record is a turnaround, not a compounder. The bank lost IDR-789.1bn in FY2022 and IDR-573.2bn in FY2023, broke even in FY2024 at IDR19.9bn, and earned IDR565.7bn in FY2025 [S0][S19]. The swing came from efficiency and asset quality: BOPO fell to 84.2% from 99.3% [S19], NIM held at 14.4%, CIR held near a third of total operating income as reported, and NPL net fell to 0.9% [S19]. Total assets reached IDR18,973.8bn and equity IDR4,230.7bn [S0].

Momentum has flattened, and we say so. 9M2026 profit after tax was IDR431.0bn, below the IDR464.0bn earned in 9M2025 [S2][S11], and the third quarter alone was well below its 2025 level. Cost and margin were not the cause: NII rose every quarter to IDR576.0bn in Q3 and BOPO improved year on year [S2]. The shortfall therefore sits below pre-provision profit, in provisioning, which the press release does not break out. Our FY2026E of IDR551.3bn needs a Q4 close to the Q3 run-rate rather than the weak Q4-2025 base, so it requires no growth on the latest quarter; a Q4 at the Q3 level delivers it.

Our revenue build starts from a smaller balance sheet. We model FY2026E loans at IDR6,730.5bn, held at the September-2026 level of IDR6,730.0bn [S2] rather than rebuilt in Q4: the commercial book is still being reduced [S21] and Q4-2025 loans contracted into year-end [S19], so a Q4 pickup is not the base case — it is upside to the NII line, not an assumption. Deposits fall to IDR12,907.6bn as management reprices expensive time deposits, then grow with the loan book from FY2027E. The margin needs a word on bases: the company reports NIM of 14.4% on productive assets [S19], while the engine applies NII to total assets, where FY2025 NII of IDR2,348.8bn on assets of IDR18,973.8bn is a little above the 9M2026 total-asset rate, not below it. That total-asset margin is held near flat and edged up to 12.3% by FY2035E as loans grow inside an earning-asset base carried at a constant 2.6 times loans, not cut toward a sector average and not lifted by a separate balance-sheet assumption [S19][S2]. Non-interest income grows from a small base, and the cost-to-income ratio improves from 73.0% to 64.0% as the platform scales [S19][S2].

Credit cost is the most important forecast choice. FY2025 and 9M2026 provisioning was close to zero in the reported numbers, with NPL gross at 2.8% and NPL net at 0.9% [S2][S19]. We do not extrapolate that: the base case lifts credit cost to 1.2% in FY2027E and 2.5% by FY2030E, a through-cycle assumption for a book that is mostly unsecured consumer and UMKM. That is deliberately above the latest actual, per the house rule that below-cycle provisioning is earnings borrowed from the future, and it sits between the near-zero actual and the house assumption for the closest digital peer; the higher case is our bear.

The funding side is where the model earns its keep. Deposits of IDR14,030.0bn against loans of IDR7,180.0bn leave an LDR of 51.2% and a large liquidity buffer, with LCR reported at a very high level and securities and cash carrying the excess [S19]. That structure is cheap in a crisis and expensive in the P&L: idle liquidity earns the policy rate rather than a consumer-loan yield, which is why the NIM can be high while the ROA is modest. As the loan book is rebuilt from FY2027E, the mix shift should lift earning-asset yield without new capital, because the capital and the deposits are already there. Our forecast carries earning assets at a constant 2.6 times loans, so NII builds with the loan book rather than with an unstated second balance sheet.

The forecast path through FY2030E is deliberately unheroic. Revenue grows from the NII base as loans recover, non-interest income compounds from a small base, and cost-to-income improves only as fast as the platform's operating leverage allows, not as fast as the reported CIR implies [S19][S2]. Profit after tax rises from IDR551.3bn in FY2026E to IDR784.3bn in FY2030E, with book value per share compounding from Rp358 to Rp535. Dividends begin in FY2028E and reach 60.0% of earnings, so the compounding is visible in book value before it is visible in cash returns.

Capital adequacy is not a forecast variable in this model because it is not a constraint. CAR of 53.4% and core capital of IDR4,350.0bn mean the binding constraint on growth is credit demand and underwriting capacity, not regulatory capital [S2]. We therefore hold share count constant and model no rights issue; The risk is the reverse, that excess capital dilutes ROE until it is either deployed or returned: CAR of 53.4% against a conservative core equity tier one target leaves a large capital surplus above requirement, a material share of equity, which the bank can return without constraining growth [S2][S19]. The LDR of 51.2% and the very high reported LCR confirm the bank could grow loans substantially without new capital [S2][S19]. The constraint is demand and credit quality, not solvency. RWA density is about 1.1 times loans, consistent with the reported CAR and the loan book [S19].

Earnings-quality flags. For a bank the accruals screen is replaced by provisioning and write-off trends. Here the flag is not fabricated revenue but a very low provision charge against a gross NPL ratio in the high twos: reported profit is real cash earnings, but it is flattered by a benign credit cycle [S19][S2]. The related-party channel is the controlling shareholder's ecosystem, which we cannot quantify from the public sources reviewed; that is a genuine information gap [S6]. No special-monitoring-board status or special notation letter was disclosed in the sources we reviewed [S0]. The zero dividend is a capital-retention decision, not an accounting flag [S8][S12]. Tax is charged at 10.0% even though FY2025 cash tax was a small credit and the FY2022 and FY2023 losses leave carryforwards; the engine floors the rate at that level, so we overstate tax by roughly the carryforward period, a small conservative bias we accept and disclose.

A bank is valued on its book value and the return it earns on that book, not on a free-cash-flow multiple: deposits and loans are the raw material, and the equity base is the capital that supports them. We therefore use the house bank method set — residual income as the engine, justified P/BV as the cross-check and DDM as the dividend-only floor — with COE pinned to the local sovereign curve plus an equity risk premium. The IDR cost of equity is 11.9%: a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign default spread of 1.6%, a mature ERP of 4.2%, an Indonesia country premium of 2.5% and an unlevered beta of 0.90 (levering is neutral because we carry no debt weight), with no debt weight because a bank's leverage is already inside its ROE [S0].

The residual-income engine gives Rp347 per share: opening equity of the September-2026 balance sheet plus the present value of every year's profit above the cost of equity, including a terminal value at 4.7% growth. The cross-check is warranted P/BV: at a sustainable ROE of 11.4%, a COE of 11.9% and terminal growth of 4.7%, the warranted multiple is 0.9x, applied to the reported September-2026 book, giving Rp321. The DDM gives Rp364, 13.4% versus the cross-check, because it values only the dividend stream and the bank pays nothing until FY2028E.

The DDM now converges with the residual-income engine because the payout path rises to 60.0%. That path is our forecast, not a management commitment: only the FY2025 full retention is sourced [S8][S12], no dividend policy or timeline has been disclosed [S8][S2], and the DDM carries a minority weight in the blend — so a path that stayed at zero would cut the DDM toward the dividend-only floor and move the blended target, which is why we show the payout path as a judgement rather than a fact. The useful read is the other way round: ROE is 12.2% in FY2026E and settles near 11.6% by FY2035E, against a 11.9% COE. ROE sits at, not above, the cost of equity, so retention neither creates nor destroys much value at the margin and the fundamental value converges on book. That is why the methods cluster near book rather than diverging; the market at a fraction of book is the anomaly, not our value. The bear case is where the dividend-only view wins.

The terminal triple is consistent after the correction. We grow the terminal value at 4.7%, which is the retention-implied rate: a 60.0% payout from FY2031E leaves the balance of the 11.6% terminal ROE retained, and that retention times the ROE equals the 4.7% we discount. The payout path reaches 60.0% from FY2031E, not FY2030E, where it is still 45.0%; the earlier draft rounded that forward a year and used a terminal growth below the retention-implied rate, and both are fixed here. The cross-check multiple uses the average ROE of the first three forecast years, which is above the terminal ROE, and we disclose that rather than override it. On the terminal ROE alone the warranted multiple would be below book, which brackets the blend from below. The capital-return path is where the excess capital shows up: at a CAR of 53.4% the bank can distribute without constraining growth, and every point of payout at a price below book is accretive to per-share value [S2]. Strategic or control value is excluded on purpose: Akulaku already controls the bank and no bid or price has been disclosed, so any take-out premium would be speculation; a transaction at book would imply roughly the cross-check value, but it is not in our number [S6][S4].

What today's price implies. At 0.4x times FY2026E book, the market is capitalising a sustainable ROE far below the 12.2% we forecast — roughly two-thirds of it, an implied return on book well short of the cost of equity — close to the dividend-only value and below any ROE the bank has earned since 2025. The reverse read is that a re-rating to the warranted multiple is the entire return; we do not need earnings growth beyond the base case to justify the target. The risk to that view is governance and control, which is where the discount is probably rooted.

Regulatory and compliance risk is material. The bank operates under OJK and Bank Indonesia, and any fit-and-proper, marketing-partner or governance finding carries franchise and reputation cost even when the core licence is untouched. The March 2026 OJK decision cancelling a marketing-partner registration is the recent example; the bank said operations continued normally [S23]. We treat it as optics-class, not manipulation-class, but it reinforces the governance discount.

Credit risk is the largest earnings risk. The loan book is unsecured consumer and UMKM credit, where a benign NPL ratio can turn quickly. NPL gross was 2.8% at Sep-2026 and NPL net 0.9% in FY2025 [S2][S19]; a move back toward the FY2024 stress levels would break the earnings base. Our bear case lifts the through-cycle cost of risk, takes NPL gross well above the current level, reverses part of the CASA gain, cuts the total-asset margin and stops loan growth; it produces a value below today's price, which is what a bear case should do. The severe-outcome claim is withdrawn: at the current price the market is discounting a permanent ROE below the cost of equity, not a credit cycle.

Funding and macro risk are second-order but real. Deposit competition and the BI rate path determine the NIM; the house macro deck has the policy rate at 5.8% [S0], and a renewed tightening cycle would squeeze a small CASA franchise first. Currency is not a direct earnings driver because the book is rupiah-denominated, but a weaker rupiah raises imported technology costs and can force a higher risk premium on Indonesian equities.

Governance and control risk is the swing factor. The Akulaku group controls the bank [S6], Gozco is a large minority holder [S5], and the free float is 48.3% [S0]. The controller's intentions — whether it stays, sells down or injects capital — can dominate the fundamental value in the next year. Management turnover is high: a new president director and compliance director took office at the end of October 2026 [S6][S22]. The zero dividend keeps the DDM value low and the stock dependent on a re-rating rather than income, but it is a capital-retention choice by a bank with a CAR of 53.4%, not a legal block [S8][S2].

Liquidity risk is low. LDR is 51.2%, LCR was reported at a very high level, and the capital surplus is large [S19]. The shares are liquid enough for the house: three-month average daily turnover is IDR8.7bn [S0].

Structural and competitive risk sits underneath the cyclical ones. A digital bank with a narrow moat has to keep spending to defend its app engagement, and the cost line is the first place that shows it; the reported BOPO improvement is real but it came partly from cutting the loan book, and rebuilding growth will test whether the cost discipline survives [S19][S2]. Deposit competition from larger banks and digital peers is the second channel: CASA of 33.0% is an improvement, not a fortress, and a rate war would hit the NIM before it hit volumes [S2][S21]. Neither risk is in our bear case as a separate shock, because both travel through the NIM and credit-cost assumptions we already stress.

Our probabilities are 50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull. Both cases carry the same number of shocks. The credit-cost shock is mirrored; the margin, loan-growth and deposit-growth shocks are not, because a bank at a fraction of book re-rating toward book captures most of the upside while a credit cycle can halve book value — the asymmetry is sourced in the ROE-versus-COE arithmetic, not in optimism [S2][S19]. The signposts that would change our view: NPL gross through 2.8% with provisioning rising faster than loans; CASA falling below a third of deposits; a controller sell-down or a capital injection at a premium; and a first dividend or capital-return announcement.

Ownership is concentrated. The Akulaku group is the controlling shareholder [S6]; Gozco Capital held 10.5% in Feb-2026 [S5]; the free float is 48.3% [S0], with the balance held by the Akulaku group and Gozco. The board was reshuffled at an extraordinary general meeting on 29 October 2026: Christian Lesmana became president director and Yosea Iskandar compliance director [S6]. Inkawan D. Jusi continues as Komisaris Utama, an independent position he already held in May-2026, with Pramoda Dei Sudarmo as the independent commissioner [S8][S22]. The new team's mandate is explicitly governance, decision-making and risk mitigation, which is the right response to the discount but also a signal that the prior setup was found wanting.

Related-party exposure runs through the controller's ecosystem. A digital bank controlled by a fintech group naturally lends through, or alongside, that group's platform; we could not quantify the share of loans or fees from the public sources reviewed, and we flag that as an open diligence item rather than assume it away [S6][S0]. There were no pledged-share disclosures in the sources reviewed [S0]. The auditor and audit opinion were not available in the documents we could retrieve.

The board has an independent president commissioner in place since May-2026 and a further independent commissioner, with a dedicated compliance director added in October [S8][S22]. That is the structure a bank needs, but the improvement is mostly continuity rather than a new October-2026 separation of duties. It does not by itself answer the related-party question, which needs disclosure rather than organisation charts.

Capital allocation is conservative. FY2025 profit of IDR565.7bn was fully retained, with no dividend, to rebuild capital and support growth [S8]. The bank's capital ratios are far above regulatory minima [S2]. Dividends are therefore a future event, not a current return: our model starts a payout in FY2028E at 15.0% and lifts it to 45.0% by FY2030E. The net dividend yield in the twelve-month valuation is Rp0, so the return is capital appreciation, not income.

ESG exposure is mostly social and governance, not environmental. Digital inclusion and access to finance are positive social contributors; cybersecurity, data privacy and responsible lending are the material risks. The new management's emphasis on risk and compliance is the right signal, but the governance history — controller concentration and board turnover — is why the bear case carries the downside rather than a higher base-case COE. The OJK marketing-partner registration that was cancelled had never been launched, so we do not use it as evidence of an operating failure, only as a supervisory signal [S23].

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 results in the first quarter of 2027, the AGM decision on FY2026 profit in May 2027, OJK fit-and-proper approval of the new directors, and the BNPL and fee-income ramp through 2027 [S19][S22][S8]. The single most important non-dated catalyst is any change in the controller's stake.

Between updates we monitor: loan growth and the consumer/UMKM mix; NIM and CASA ratio; BOPO/CIR; credit cost and NPL gross/net; CAR and core capital; and the dividend policy [S19][S2]. The key threshold is provisioning: if credit cost stays near zero while loans grow again, the quality of the earnings is improving; if it stays near zero while NPL gross rises, the earnings are borrowed [S19][S21].

The valuation is a balance-sheet call with an earnings normalisation, so the monitoring list is short and credit-led [S19][S2]. We would revisit the rating if NPL gross moved materially above the current level with coverage falling, if CASA reversed, or if the controller sold down at a price that reset the market's view of fair value [S2][S6].

bear.narrative: The unsecured book seasons as it did in FY2022-23: NPL gross pushes above 5%, the through-cycle cost of risk reaches 3.5%, CASA reverses as depositors chase rates and loan growth stalls, so book value compounds slowly and the warranted multiple falls toward the low end of the range.

bull.narrative: The consumer/UMKM book and BNPL scale without seasoning, CASA holds near a third of deposits and the cost base stays flat, so ROE holds near 15% on a larger book — roughly 1.6x book, above the 11.85% COE — and the 53% CAR is partly returned through a special dividend or buyback, lifting book value per share and the multiple.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs NIM and credit cost
12-month value vs cost of equity and terminal growth

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E holds gross loans at the September-2026 actual of Rp6.73trn (F16) with no Q4 rebuild, because Q4-2025 loans fell about 4% and the commercial/corporate book is still being reduced; FY2027E+ resumes low-single-digit growth as the consumer/UMKM book (Rp5.80trn, +6.68% yoy in 1H2026) is prioritised [S2][S21].

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: DPK Rp11.86trn at Sep-2026, down 12.9% yoy as management deliberately repriced time deposits lower; FY2026E -8% with a Q4 pickup, then growth tracks the loan book. CASA ratio improved to 33.05% (from 28.40%), limiting the funding-cost damage.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: Earning assets are carried on the total-assets base: FY2025 total assets Rp18.97trn over loans Rp7.18trn is 2.64x [S19]. The company's reported 14.39% NIM is struck on productive assets only, so the margin input below is NII divided by total assets (12.4% in FY2025) to keep one consistent base.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: NII on total assets: FY2025 NII Rp2.35trn over total assets Rp18.97trn is 12.38%, and 9M2026 NII Rp1.69trn runs at Rp2.25trn annualised, 12.1% of the total-asset base. Held near 12.1% and edged up to 12.3% as the loan share of assets rises from a 53% LDR [S19][S2]; the company's 14.30-14.39% NIM is on productive assets, a smaller base.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Fee income +5.67% yoy in 9M2026 to Rp90.55bn on QRIS and transaction growth; small base and BNPL launch support low-double-digit growth, easing to 8% in the long run.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: Opex/TOI derived from the BOPO formula: FY2025 BOPO 84.18% gives opex ~Rp1.99trn or 75% of TOI, and 9M2026 BOPO improved to 81.77% from 82.81%, about 73% on 9M TOI. Modelled to keep improving with operating leverage on a flat cost base; the reported 31% CIR uses a different denominator and is not comparable.

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2025 and 9M2026 provisioning was near zero with NPL gross falling to 2.78% and NPL net 0.89%; the base case normalises to a 2.5% through-cycle cost of risk by FY2030E, between the near-zero actual and the 4.5% house assumption for the closest digital peer, because two-thirds of the book is consumer/UMKM and the FY2022-23 losses show how fast unsecured credit turns. FY2026E stays at the 0.5% run-rate the 9M accounts show.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero: FY2025 non-operating items were small relative to TOI and no recurring item is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory 22%, but the FY2022-23 losses leave loss carryforwards and FY2025 cash tax was a small credit; the engine floors the effective rate at 10%, so the model charges 10% from FY2026E, roughly two years earlier than the carryforward expiry. The overstatement is small relative to value and is disclosed in section 3.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interests in the consolidated accounts.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 profit was fully retained by the May-2026 RUPST to strengthen the capital structure [S8][S12]. With CAR at 53.4% and core capital Rp4.35trn [S2] against a mid-teens CET1 need, payout starts at 15% in FY2028E, 30% in FY2029E, 45% in FY2030E and reaches 60% from FY2031E. This path is an analyst forecast, not a disclosed management commitment: no dividend policy or timeline is in the filings [S8][S2]. It makes terminal growth consistent: the 60% payout leaves 40% retention on the 11.8% terminal ROE, about 4.7% growth.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or buyback announced; shares 13,350m held constant.

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: FY2025 core capital Rp4.03trn over CAR 49.07% implies RWA ~Rp8.2trn, or 1.14x loans of Rp7.18trn; 1.15x used, consistent with the 53.40% CAR at Sep-2026.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: Retention-implied terminal growth: the FY2035E terminal ROE of 11.8% with a 60% payout leaves 40% retention, giving about 4.7%, which is below the BI rate of 5.75% in the house macro deck [S0] and consistent with the terminal ROE-retention triple used in the RI, P/BV and DDM terminals.

challenges.challenge: Credit cost is the stated first driver but runs 0.5% of loans in FY2026E rising only to 1.8% by FY2030E, while house comps model 3.2% (BBRI), 4.5% (ARTO) and 6.4% (BBHI) for comparable consumer/unsecured books and BBYB own FY2022-23 losses (-789bn, -573bn) imply a far higher loss rate.
challenges.answer: Credit cost is now a 2.5% through-cycle charge by FY2030E, up from 1.8%, anchored on NPL gross 2.78% and NPL net 0.89% [S2][S19] and set below the house digital-peer assumption because the commercial book is being cut; the 3.5% case is the bear.

challenges.challenge: The bear adds 60bp credit cost, 40bp NIM and 3pp growth and returns Rp232, 48% above the Rp157 price, so the claim that the stock is priced for a severe outcome is unsupported; the bear narrative itself says NPL gross pushes above 4%, for which 60bp of CoR is far too small, and the FY2022-23 loss precedent implies 3-5% CoR and roughly 0.25-0.3x book (Rp85-110).
challenges.answer: The bear is rebuilt on the loss history: cost of risk one point higher through the cycle (3.5% terminal), NPL gross above 5%, a CASA/deposit reversal and loan growth stopped; it now values the bank below the current price, and the severe-outcome sentence is deleted.

challenges.challenge: Earnings momentum is negative and unmentioned: 9M2026 PAT Rp430.98bn is -7.1% yoy vs Rp464bn [S2][S11] and Q3-2026 alone is Rp136.1bn vs Rp187.9bn (-27.6% yoy); the report frames 9M2026 only as strengthening, and flat FY2026E Rp564.3bn needs Q4 of Rp133.4bn, +31% yoy on Q4-2025 of Rp101.7bn.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states the 9M2026 profit decline versus 9M2025, shows that NII rose each quarter and BOPO improved [S2], locates the shortfall below pre-provision profit in provisioning, and shows FY2026E needs only a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate.

challenges.challenge: The largest lever is absent: CAR 53.4% and core capital Rp4.35trn [S2] against a 20-25% CET1 need leaves roughly Rp2.5-3trn of excess capital, and at 0.44x book a buyback or special dividend is strongly accretive to BVPS; the model caps payout at 30% with no buyback and the bull case shocks only CoR, NIM and growth.
challenges.answer: Excess capital is quantified against a conservative CET1 target in section 4, the payout path now rises to 60% and the bull narrative carries the special dividend/buyback; bank methods capitalise equity directly so a bridge add-on would double count.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 concedes that controller intentions can dominate the fundamental value, yet no scenario, bridge item or bull shock prices a control transaction, a parent loan-book injection or a take-out; the house news of 2026-11-10 has a consortium acquiring BBKP, and S4 (Akulaku buying BBYB) sits in the source list unused.
challenges.answer: Strategic value is now explicitly excluded with the reason: Akulaku already controls the bank and no bid or price is disclosed [S6][S4]; section 4 states what a transaction at book would imply but keeps it out of the number.

challenges.challenge: VAL_BANKS names residual income the engine and warranted P/BV the cross-check; the report inverts them (P/BV 50%, RI 30%, DDM 20%) without the explicit argument the card requires, and the inverted primary (Rp324) is 24% above the RI (Rp262), so the weighting alone adds about Rp31 per share to the blend.
challenges.answer: The weights are re-set to the VAL_BANKS hierarchy: residual income 50%, justified P/BV 30%, DDM 20%; the target and rating are re-run on the card weights.

challenges.challenge: The section 4 inputs do not produce its output: it says sustainable ROE 11.5%, warranted P/BV 1.0x and BVPS Rp359 give Rp324, but 1.0x on 359 is 359 and (11.5-4)/(11.85-4) is 0.96x, or Rp343; the engine actually uses ROE 11.46%, P/BV 0.950x and BVPS Rp341.08 (current reported book, not FY2026E Rp359). The same paragraph says ROE 11.2% vs COE 11.9% means retention creates value at the margin, which is the opposite of true when ROE is below COE.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now reports the engine's own inputs: book value per share from the September-2026 balance sheet, 0.95x warranted P/BV, sustainable ROE of the first forecast years; the incorrect claim that retention creates value below COE is replaced with ROE at, not above, COE.

challenges.challenge: The terminal triple is inconsistent: FY2035E ROE 9.8% with 30% payout implies 6.9% sustainable growth, yet terminal growth is 4.0%, so the model retains capital that neither grows nor is distributed, while the primary method silently overrides the terminal ROE upward to 11.46%.
challenges.answer: The terminal triple is made consistent: payout reaches 60%, terminal ROE is near the model path and growth is 4%, so retention times ROE equals g; the cross-check multiple's use of the higher first-years ROE is disclosed rather than overridden, and the terminal-ROE multiple is shown below book.

challenges.challenge: F15 records earning_assets FY2025A as 18,970, but the cited quote says total aset Rp18,97 triliun [S20] and the analyst basis note says the 14.39% NIM implies earning assets of about Rp16.3trn; the model therefore averages 18,970 with FY2026E 15,891, giving FY2026E NII of Rp2,475bn against an annualised 9M2026 run-rate of Rp2,263bn [S2, NII Rp1.69trn], a 9.4% overstatement, and an NII path of +5.4% in FY2026 then -7.9% in FY2027 while loans go -2.5% then +5%.
challenges.answer: F15 is relabelled as the total-asset anchor because earning assets are not separately disclosed [S20]; earning assets per loan are now 2.64x, matching that base, and the margin input is NII over total assets, so FY2026E NII is 2,266 against the 9M2026 run-rate rather than 2,475.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says At Sep-2026 gross loans were IDR7,180.0bn, but S2 has Rp6.73trn at Sep-2026 (-10.2% yoy) and Rp7.18trn is the Dec-2025 figure [S19]; it also says consumer and UMKM lending reached IDR3,500.0bn in savings-funded CASA, conflating savings deposits of Rp3.50trn [S19] with the consumer/UMKM loan book of Rp5.80trn [S21].
challenges.answer: Section 1 now uses Sep-2026 loans of Rp6.73trn and Sep-2026 deposits of Rp11.86trn [S2], and the consumer/UMKM book is the Rp5.80trn Jun-2026 figure [S21], not the savings balance.

challenges.challenge: The valuation rests on an unverified equity base: S3/S15/S16/S17 (annual-report pages) captured only site navigation and S15/S16/S17 are byte-identical 2,506-byte shells, so equity Rp4,230.7bn, total assets Rp18,973.8bn, NII Rp2,348.8bn and therefore BVPS Rp341 all come from Yahoo [S0] and news wires, with no LK, no notes, no audit opinion, no loan-loss coverage and no related-party disclosure, for a bank whose profit rose 2,745% on near-zero provisions.
challenges.answer: The report discloses that the annual-report pages captured only navigation shells and that equity, provisions and BVPS rest on Yahoo and press reports, with book value corroborated by core capital of Rp4.35trn [S2]; the multiple is left at 0.95x but the rating's dependence on unverified book is stated.

challenges.challenge: The accumulated deficit appears six times and drives the payout path, the DDM floor and the deficit-clearing catalyst, but no cited source states it: S8 and S12 say the FY2025 profit was retained to strengthen the capital structure (memperkuat struktur modal), not to clear a deficit, and the drift.payout QC justification cites S8/S13 for a two-year dividend timeline that neither article states.
challenges.answer: Every accumulated-deficit claim is removed: the sources say FY2025 profit was booked as retained earnings to strengthen capital, not to clear a deficit [S8][S12]; the payout basis, DDM path and catalyst are rewritten and the model re-run.

challenges.challenge: Two unsourced conservative drifts: NIM is cut from 14.30% at 9M2026 (flat vs 14.39% FY2025, CASA +465bp) to 12.0% by FY2035, about Rp500bn of FY2035 NII and the largest haircut in the model; and tax is charged at 10% (about 11% of NP) although the model concedes FY2025 tax was about zero and that loss carryforwards exist, the same deficit that supposedly blocks dividends, so it is certain for payouts but ignored for tax.
challenges.answer: The NIM cut is gone: the model now measures NII on total assets, where FY2025 is 12.38% and the path holds near 12.1-12.3%, with the company's productive-asset NIM disclosed as a different base [S19][S2]; the 10% tax floor and carryforward overstatement are disclosed in section 3.

challenges.challenge: Visible errors overstate the case: market cap IDR2,096,025,728,322.0bn and turnover IDR8,723,651,652.4bn (unit slips); probabilities stated as 0.5% base, 0.2% bear and 0.2% bull (sums to 0.9, and the model is 50/25/25); bear credit cost 0.5% vs 0.6% modelled; policy rate 5.8% vs the deck 5.75%; insiders at 58.9% alongside a 48.3% free float, which are mutually exclusive; and a 0.0% liquidity discount on Rp8.7bn ADTV (0.4% of market cap).
challenges.answer: Market cap and turnover now render in billions, scenario probabilities use the fraction format, the bear text no longer cites the base-case credit cost, insider and float figures no longer overlap, and the zero liquidity discount is justified against ADTV [S0].

challenges.challenge: The governance section overstates both the improvement and the OJK event: it calls Inkawan D. Jusi an independent president commissioner as a new October-2026 appointment, but S22 lists him as Komisaris Utama with Pramoda Dei Sudarmo as Komisaris Independen, and S8 already named him Komisaris Utama Independen in May-2026, so the clearer separation of duties is not new; it also omits that the OJK-cancelled marketing-partner programme had never been launched [S23] while using the event to support a governance discount.
challenges.answer: The board description is corrected: Inkawan D. Jusi continues as Komisaris Utama, independent since May-2026, with Pramoda Dei Sudarmo as independent commissioner [S8][S22]; the cancelled marketing-partner programme is stated never to have launched [S23] and the discount is re-tested against the bear case.

missing_bull_case.note: Bull case shocks only CoR/NIM/growth; omits the buyback or special dividend that 0.44x book and 53% CAR make highly accretive, a control/M&A premium, and NIM persistence at 14.3%; section 5 itself says control can dominate value.

missing_bear_case.note: Bear is Rp232, 48% above the Rp157 price, so the severe-outcome claim is unsupported; it omits the Q3-2026 -28% yoy PAT decline, the FY2022-23 loss precedent and unquantified related-party and pledge risk.

assumption_realism.note: Credit cost 1.8% long-run vs peers 3.2-6.4% (BBRI, ARTO, BBHI); NIM cut 230bp with no source; tax 10% vs about zero actual; FY2026E Q4 loans +4.0% contradicts Q4-2025 -4.1%; payout and deficit unsourced.

evidence_and_citations.note: F15 records total assets as earning assets; section 1 misdates loans and conflates savings deposits with the loan book; S15-S17 are byte-identical navigation shells, so no LK, audit opinion or notes; the accumulated deficit is cited six times but no source states it.

valuation_method_fit.note: Warranted P/BV made primary inverts VAL_BANKS, which names residual income the engine; section 4 inputs (1.0x, Rp359) do not reproduce Rp324 (engine 0.95x, Rp341); terminal g 4% vs ROE 9.8% x 70% retention = 6.9%; ROE override to 11.46% undisclosed.

bias_and_tone.note: Priced-for-a-severe-outcome is contradicted by a bear 48% above price; retention is said to create value while ROE (11.2%) sits below COE (11.9%); the governance discount leans on a never-launched programme; unit, probability and ownership errors.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: COE 11.85% matches the house default (rf 7.45%, spread 1.62%, beta 0.9, ERP 4.23 plus CRP 2.46) and peers; the BI path of 5.75% is used in the terminal note; only the 5.8% prose slip.

conservatism_audit.note: Two unsourced haircuts, NIM 14.30% to 12.0% and tax at 10% vs about zero paid, partly offset by optimistic Q4 loan and deposit pickups, a 0.0% liquidity discount and the ROE override in the primary method.

calibration.note: FY2026E NP 564.3 vs 565.7 actual reproduces the economics and the -2.0pp ROE gap is equity growth (+13.3%) not drift, but it is never explained and the calibration actual 14.52% is not the LK reported 15.13% [S19].

signoff.notes: APPROVED 2026-11-11. Target reproduces exactly: RI 347 (50%) + justified P/BV 321 (30%) + DDM 364 (20%) = 343, rolled one year at COE 11.85% = 383 base, probability-weighted 50/25/25 on 383/135/601 = 376 (+139.3% vs Rp157, 0.44x FY2026E book). The return is a re-rating, not an earnings-growth aspiration: ROE 12.2% FY2026E settling 11.6% against an 11.9% COE makes value converge on book (warranted P/B about 1.0x on the first-three-year average ROE, 0.94x on the terminal ROE), so the +139pc is the gap between a 0.44x price and a ~1.0x warranted multiple on Rp358 next-year book. Every departure from the last actual runs against us: credit cost lifts from ~0.5pc to 2.5pc through-cycle, tax is charged at a 10pc floor, NIM is held at the total-asset realised rate rather than the reported productive-asset 14.4pc base, and the 9M2026 profit decline of -7.1pc yoy is stated in section 3. Bear 25pc at Rp135 sits below the price, so the distribution is not one-sided. Batch check on BANKS comps: ratings span SELL/REDUCE/BUY on both sides of price with no shared input driving the tape; BBYB is the outlier on the upside for a sourced reason, its ROE at the deepest P/BV (0.44x vs 0.58x NOBU, 0.72x BNBA, 1.2-1.7x BBRI/BBHI/BBMD/BMAS), coherent with ROE-to-warranted-multiple logic rather than a template tilt. Q12 and Q13 do not block: the deposit line (FY2026E Rp12,907.6bn, +8.8pc on the Sep-2026 Rp11,860bn while loans are held flat) is presentational because NII is struck on total assets with earning assets at 2.64x loans, so deposits enter no cash-flow or discount input and the inconsistency cannot move the rating; Q13 (no deposit beta or CASA-TD path against the BI 5.75pc path) is a card-completeness gap on a name the report explicitly frames as a balance-sheet-value call rather than a NIM-beta trade, with NIM a level input not a transmission coefficient. Both to be fixed at the next refresh; neither is a valuation error. Governance and control discount persistence is the live risk to 12-month convergence and is disclosed in sections 4 and 6.

bias.note: Base case anchors on the FY2025 actual and the Sept-2026 balance sheet: FY2026E ROE 12.2% against 15.1% actual [S19] is supported by 9M2026 PAT Rp431.0bn, -7.1% yoy [S2][S11]; NII on total assets stays at 12.1-12.3% against 12.38% FY2025, no unexplained NIM haircut beyond 28bp; loans held at the Rp6.73trn Sep-2026 actual with the Q4 pickup treated as upside. Credit cost normalised to 2.5% through-cycle per VAL_BANKS, offset by a 73% to 62% CTI path sourced to BOPO 99.34 to 84.18 to 81.77 [S19][S2] and a 60% terminal payout. Conservatism (10% tax floor, 0% payout to FY2027E, terminal g 4.7% below BI 5.75%) and optimism (60% payout from FY2031E, 2.64x earning assets vs 2.55x actual) are both disclosed. Scenarios 50/25/25 with the same four shocks, asymmetries justified in qc_justifications.

recomputed.item: FY2026E total assets vs Sep-2026 actual

findings.finding: The deposit path is inconsistent with the loan convention. FY2026E deposits of Rp12,907.6bn is -8.0% yoy but +8.8% on the Sept-2026 actual of Rp11,860bn [S2], i.e. a Rp1,048bn Q4-2026 deposit build, while loans are deliberately held flat at the Sept actual and the text calls a Q4 loan pickup 'upside, not base'. Section 3 presents the line only as a repricing decline and does not disclose the Q4 build.

VAL_BANKS output contract requires the deposit beta and the CASA/TD mix path against the BI path; the report states CASA 33.05% at Sept-2026 [S2] but gives no deposit beta and no CASA/TD path against the house BI path of 5.75%, for a bank whose risk case is a small-CASA funding squeeze.

Earning assets are carried at 2.64x loans in every year, but the Sept-2026 accounts show total assets of Rp17,190bn on loans of Rp6,730bn, 2.55x [S2]; FY2026E total assets of Rp17,786bn is therefore 3.5% above the actual. Under the 5% threshold but it overstates the generated balance sheet and NII slightly.

Section 3 says the cost-to-income ratio improves 'from 73.0% to 64.0%' alongside a path that runs to FY2035E; 64.0% is the FY2030E value and the model reaches 62.0% from FY2031E. Terminal NIM is likewise 12.3% versus the 12.38% FY2025 actual.

Judge NOTE, accepted: the implied sustainable ROE at 0.44x FY2026E book, 11.85% COE and 4.7% g is about 7.9%, and section 4 calls that 'roughly two-thirds' of 12.2% without printing the number, then compares it to the 'dividend-only value' which is Rp364, far above the price [S2][S19].
Judge NOTE, accepted: ownership disclosures still sum past 100% - insiders 58.9% and free float 48.3% [S0] - and section 6 still says the balance is held by Akulaku plus Gozco.

flags.message: a.cti moves -11.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The 13pp improvement from 75% to 62% is the operating leverage already visible in the accounts: BOPO fell from 99.34% in FY2024 to 84.18% in FY2025 and 81.77% at 9M2026 while TOI held, so opex/TOI declines as the digital platform scales [S19][S2].

flags.message: a.payout moves +60.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Payout stays at zero through FY2027E because the May-2026 RUPST booked all FY2025 profit as retained earnings to strengthen the capital structure [S8][S12]; dividends then start at 15% in FY2028E and rise to 60% from FY2030E on CAR of 53.4% and core capital of Rp4.35trn [S2], well above the mid-teens CET1 a digital bank needs. No source states an accumulated deficit or a two-year dividend timeline, so neither is claimed.

flags.message: a.deposit_growth: bear -0.05 vs bull 0.03 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: Deliberately lopsided and sourced: the bear assumes a CASA reversal of five percentage points because the high CASA ratio is the funding shock channel for a small digital bank [S2], while the bull assumes only a partial hold because deposits already exceed loans, so deposit growth is not the binding driver of upside [S19].

flags.message: a.loan_growth: bear -0.1 vs bull 0.04 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: Deliberately lopsided and sourced: the bear cuts loan growth hard because a credit cycle stops the unsecured book, which fell sharply in FY2025 [S19]; the bull adds a smaller amount because the bank restarted from a deliberately shrinking book and the consumer/UMKM segment is growing slowly [S21].

flags.message: a.nim: bear -0.01 vs bull 0.005 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: Deliberately lopsided and sourced: the bear cuts the total-asset margin by a full point because a deposit-rate war hits a small CASA franchise before volumes [S2], while the bull adds half a point because the margin is already near its reported level with a low LDR and room to redeploy liquidity into loans [S19].

flags.message: expected return +139%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return rests on three sourced drivers: (1) the shares trade near 0.45x reported book of Rp341 per share against a residual-income value that already assumes a 2.5% through-cycle cost of risk and a total-asset margin below the reported NIM [S19][S2]; (2) FY2025 net profit of Rp565.69bn is cash-generative with CAR at 53.4% and core capital of Rp4.35trn [S2][S19]; (3) at the current price the market capitalises a sustainable ROE close to the dividend-only value, far below the 11-13% the franchise earns on book [S2][S21]. The bear case is now a genuine below-price outcome.
